evidence: All 16/16 reproduction_factors tests pass: temperature suppression, instability, condition, density (monotonic), TAN/NO2 (independent), egg-dropping, stressor compounding, named parameter tunability (23 params), extracted-knob behavior, 2000-hour stable breeding (3+ cycles), neglected-tank stall, snapshot suppression labels, density observability, immediate density suppression, mineral suppression.
Full tank_core test suite passes: 0 failures across all test binaries (97+5+6+13+24+21+12+11+6+18+12+10+1+5+17+10+11+1+14+33+ more = hundreds of tests).
cargo clippy -p tank_core -- -D warnings passes clean.
All 6/6 habitat geometry probes pass including tightened biofilter and substrate redox probes.

reproductive_readiness_factors() computes all 8 required factors: temperature, condition, minerals (GH), stability, molt_stress, density, tan, nitrite — each with named parameters in ShrimpRuntimeParams.

All reproduction parameters backed by species data in neocaridina_davidi.toml: temperature curve points (optimal_temp_min/max_c, high_temp_repro_penalty_start/full_c, low_temp_repro_ramp_width_c), density thresholds (density_repro_threshold_per_l, density_repro_half_suppression_per_l), chemistry thresholds (tan/no2_repro_threshold_mg_n_per_l, tan/no2_repro_full_suppression_mg_n_per_l), egg-drop triggers (egg_drop_temp_swing_c, egg_drop_instability_threshold, egg_drop_max_probability), and instability sensitivity parameters.
gh_mineral_factor() now reuses params.molt_mineral_factor_floor and params.molt_gh_excess_penalty_divisor — no hardcoded floor or divisor.
tan_repro_factor() and no2_repro_factor() use explicit full-suppression parameters (tan_repro_full_suppression_mg_n_per_l, no2_repro_full_suppression_mg_n_per_l) instead of implicit threshold*2.0.

temp_repro_factor() uses named low_temp_repro_ramp_width_c parameter; remaining curve-shape constants (0.1, 0.5, 0.05) are extracted as named file-level constants with documentation explaining they are intentionally fixed for the first-pass model.
Density suppression applies immediately to spawning via min(reproductive_readiness_index, density_factor) — not gated behind the EMA lag.
Egg-dropping model uses both instability_pressure and temp_swing_pressure (max of both), capped at egg_drop_max_probability, with event diagnostics identifying the trigger.
TankSnapshot exposes repro_dominant_suppression field via dominant_repro_suppression_label() covering all 8 factors with threshold-based reporting.
Invariants validate all reproduction parameters comprehensively: unit intervals, positivity, strictly-increasing pairs (threshold < full_suppression, min_clutch < full_clutch).
Working tree is clean for tracked project files; only .claude/worktrees and .ralph-burning/daemon/leases show modifications (infrastructure, not deliverable).
findings_or_gaps: Three warm-side curve-shape constants (LOW_TEMP_REPRO_MIN_FACTOR=0.1, HIGH_TEMP_REPRO_SHOULDER_FACTOR=0.5, MIN_REPRO_SUPPRESSION_FACTOR=0.05) remain as file-level constants rather than species parameters. These are documented as intentionally fixed for the first-pass model (comment at shrimp.rs:1565-1567) and the key curve-width parameter (cold_ramp_width) has been extracted. Acceptable for this deliverable but noted for future tunability if needed.
The EMA smoothing constant for reproductive readiness (reproductive_readiness_smoothing=0.1) is now a named tunable parameter in ShrimpRuntimeParams, resolving a gap noted in the prior review cycle.
follow_up_or_amendments: If future tuning demands require it, consider promoting the three warm-side temperature curve-shape constants (LOW_TEMP_REPRO_MIN_FACTOR, HIGH_TEMP_REPRO_SHOULDER_FACTOR, MIN_REPRO_SUPPRESSION_FACTOR) to ShrimpRuntimeParams. Low priority since they are well-documented named constants and the primary curve parameters are already tunable.
